newsitem.title: USA: Guatemala whistle-blower quits State Dept job.
newsitem.headline: Guatemala whistle-blower quits State Dept job.

text.p: A senior U.S. official punished by the Central Intelligence Agency after disclosing that a paid CIA informant may have been involved in murders in Guatemala has quit his State Department job, the department said on Tuesday.
Officials said Richard Nuccio, a senior policy adviser to the assistant secretary of state for Inter-American affairs, had resigned effective on Tuesday.

Nuccio, 49, will start working on March 2 for Sen. Robert Torricelli, the New Jersey Democrat to whom he passed information about Julio Roberto Alpirez, a Guatemalan officer on the CIA payroll, Torricelli's office said.

The allegation that Alpirez was implicated in the murder of a U.S. citizen and the death of a local guerrilla leader married to an American led President Bill Clinton in 1995 to order a review of CIA activities in Guatemala.

Then CIA director John Deutch later fired two officers in the agency's directorate of operations for failing to keep Congress "fully and currently informed" of covert operations, as required by a 1980 law.
But Deutch last December also upheld a decision to strip Nuccio of his access to data classified as "sensitive-compartmented information".
Deutch said Nuccio, a former special adviser to Clinton on Cuba and a one-time special envoy to Guatemala, could reapply for his clearance in a year.
A State Department spokesman said Nuccio's resignation was his own decision. The department had previously said Nuccio was welcome to work there as long as he wished.
The spokesman said Nuccio had "earned respect as a highly qualified Latin America expert" and had "very capably served two assistant secretaries of state".
A spokesman for Torricelli, Jim Jordan, said Nuccio would work as a special legislative assistant focusing on foreign affairs and intelligence.

"The addition of Richard Nuccio to the staff, given his experience, professionalism and ethical standing, will ensure that Senator Torricelli continues to play a lead role on this important issue," Jordan said.
Nuccio plans to give a news conference on Wednesday at the Washington office of Amnesty International, a spokeswoman for the international human rights organisation said.
